title: Fixed-point mechanism: ascent and descent
html:
Remark. Fixed-point mechanism: ascent and descent

Each step down the brane tower removes a space-like dimension through the \mathrm{SU}(2) rotation and its associated fixed-point set.

  1. Ascent (generation). Moving from M_k (\dim = 0) upward lifts the connection A to higher categorical structures via the jet prolongation (jet prolongation).
  2. Descent (projection). Moving downward, the descent homomorphism \mathfrak{d}_n (descent) acts as an algebraic filter (algebraic filter) on the level-(n{+}1) algebra. The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n annihilates the transient complement \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces)—the genuinely new modes at level n{+}1 lacking a pre-image at level n. At dimension 3 the connection is unconstrained and its holonomy genuinely non-abelian (descent reduction at dimension 3); quotienting by the Reeb flow gives the surface stratum, where the mass becomes central (descent reduction at dimension 2). At dimension 1, only the longitudinal \mathrm{U}(1) backbone remains (descent reduction). At dimension 0, even this collapses to a single fibre datum (descent reduction to zero).
  3. Round-trip involution. The composition of ascent and descent is the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution), acting on \Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_{n+1}). Its image \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} forms the stable core of the brane algebra at level n{+}1. The defining boundary \partial \mathcal{S}_n (brane boundary) marks the geometric locus where the fibrewise descent map has a non-trivial kernel.
